name: the panel is a block, not a column flex container
why: Flex items are blockified by the CSS display spec, which is what lets each adopted row keep its own inline display value (inline-flex -> flex, none stays none) and still lay out full-width. As a block, every row falls back to sitting inline beside its neighbour and the ::after hint's margin-left:auto stops right-aligning.
grep: an open row has a real bounding rect

name: row order comes from the adoption sequence, not the declared order
why: The render tail adopts in whatever order it calls the add*Button() helpers, and the keyboard-shortcuts row is adopted on the INITIAL render — so without _TOOLBAR_MENU_ROW_ORDER the View menu reads 'Keyboard shortcuts, Density, Statistics'.
grep: each menu adopts the real buttons

name: the emptiness reconcile in _orderToolbar() is disabled
why: Recorded as pass, honestly. What actually keeps a gated-off 🛠 View menu off the page is LAZY CREATION: every _ensure*Menu() call sits inside its own feature gate, so with Density, Statistics and Keyboard shortcuts all off the menu is never constructed and its button never exists. The reconcile is defence for a future call site that ensures a menu and then adopts nothing into it — cheap, and an easy mistake to make — but no fixture can distinguish it from the lazy creation in front of it.
grep: a gated-off feature leaves no empty row

name: adoption does not stamp the owner, so _toolbarInvoke() cannot find the host menu
why: data-mb-menu-owner is how both _toolbarInvoke() and _toolbarAnchorFor() resolve which menu holds a control — and how the test harness's clickToolbarItem() does, without a layout table of its own. Without it, Ctrl+D clicks a row inside a closed panel: the density pull-down opens against a ZERO rect, pinned to the top-left corner.

name: _toolbarInvoke() does not open the host menu first
why: The single reason that function exists. A row in a closed panel has a zero bounding rect, and Density and Export both position their own pull-down from it.

name: the row-activation close listener is bubble-phase again
why: densityBtn.onclick and exportBtn.onclick both begin with e.stopPropagation() — they must, or their own outside-click handler would close the pull-down they just opened — so a bubble listener never fires for exactly the two rows that need it. This is the defect the spec found on its first run.
grep: a panel opens on click and closes on Escape

name: opening a menu does not close its siblings
why: Two panels open at once overlap, and the second one's outside-click handler cannot close the first (the click is inside its own panel).
grep: opening one menu closes the other

name: the shortcut hint is appended as text instead of an attribute
why: updateBarcodeHighlightBtnState() rewrites its button's innerHTML wholesale, so an appended node would not survive it; and a hint inside textContent is the same hazard the column-header family avoids by drawing its glyphs from CSS.
grep: a row carries its shortcut hint as an attribute

name: ⚙️ and ❓ are no longer pinned last
why: _orderToolbar() replaced ensureSettingsButtonIsLast()'s pile of ad-hoc 'move X before Y' rules with one append sequence. Dropping the tail pass leaves the two pinned utilities wherever the render tail's adoption order happened to put them.
grep: each menu adopts the real buttons

name: the pinned pair keeps its own colours instead of the menus'
why: The change the user asked for, reverted. Both halves go back to their old slate/blue-grey grounds, so the pill reads as two differently-coloured buttons welded together rather than as one control.

edits.find:
default: '#ECEFF1|#263238|1px solid #B0BEC5',
            description: 'Settings button, the left half of the ⚙️❓ pill: bg|color|border'
edits.replace:
default: '#607D8B|white|1px solid #546E7A',
            description: 'Settings button, the left half of the ⚙️❓ pill: bg|color|border'

name: the flex gap is not cancelled, so the pill splits open
why: The bar is display:inline-flex with a gap between EVERY pair of children, and a flex gap cannot be suppressed for one pair. Without the negative margin the two halves sit 8px apart while still drawing their pill radii and their single hairline — which looks like two buttons that have each lost a corner.

name: both halves keep their side borders, doubling the divider
why: The defect the sort-group pill hit on its own first run: the left half's right border pairs with the right half's left border, so the seam draws at 2px against 1px outer edges. Side borders start at 0 and are re-grown for exactly this reason.

name: the run-relative cap selectors become :first-of-type/:last-of-type
why: CLAUDE.md records this for the sort group and it is the same trap here: those pseudo-classes count elements of the same TAG, and these two <button>s are neither the first nor the last button among their siblings — the fetch buttons and the two menu buttons are buttons too. The caps land on the wrong elements entirely.

name: the pill rules drop !important
why: Both buttons set border and border-radius INLINE, from uiSettingsBtnCSS()/uiHelpBtnCSS(). A normal-priority stylesheet rule cannot outrank inline, so every pill declaration is silently discarded and the two render as separate rounded buttons.

name: the gap-cancelling margin moves to the RIGHT half of the pill
why: The obvious place to put it, and how this shipped for an hour. It looks identical while the two halves share a line. The bar is flex-wrap:wrap, though, and at 1040-1080px — an ordinary window width — they land on different lines; the negative margin then pulls ❓ 8px past the bar's own left edge, i.e. content outside its container. On the LEFT half the same pull only shortens a line that has nothing after it.
